# Strict-corpus divergence baseline — jdk 25, windows
#
# GENERATED by scripts/jdk-only-strict-probes.sh --update-baseline.
# Never hand-edited: every line is a (probe, arm, section) that a real
# three-arm run measured as diverging from the HotSpot control.
#
# note: first baseline for 25-windows: the platform probe's security and agent sections converged on this run (PKCS12 setEntry, and the Windows attach provider's two natives), and the JNI section now actually runs under MSVC
#
# note: `JdkOnlyPlatformProbe/strict/vthreads` was ADDED BY HAND, and here is
# the measurement that justifies it. `--update-baseline` regenerates the whole
# set from ONE run, and the `vthreads` section is intermittent on this platform
# exactly as the 25-linux file records it being on that one. Ten three-arm runs
# on this host, same binary, same image, back to back:
#
#     divergent set                              runs
#     (none)                                       6
#     JdkOnlyPlatformProbe/strict/vthreads         3
#     JdkOnlyPlatformProbe/real/vthreads           1
#
# The generating run is the one that caught the `real` arm, so a baseline of
# exactly what it wrote would have gone red on three of the other nine — and a
# gate that flakes is a gate that gets switched off. Both arms were MEASURED
# diverging here; neither line is a guess. The divergence itself is the same
# `handoffs=61..63 / allJoined=false` under-count the 25-linux baseline carries,
# i.e. a race in the virtual-thread handoff counting, not a mode effect: it
# appears on `real` and on `strict` and it is the ONLY section that moves.
#
# Do not regenerate this file with --update-baseline and commit the result
# without re-reading this note: a clean run writes an EMPTY set, which reads as
# a tighter ratchet and is really a coin flip.
#
# The gate fails when this set GROWS. A line that stops diverging is
# reported and passes, so a fix is never blocked by the gate that
# measured it — re-freeze afterwards to keep the ratchet tight.
